posts.name: Subramanian M K (MKS)
posts.cooked:
In BPT1, Question 4, we have been asked to :

  1. “nslookup” a bunch of popular sites get their IP address
  2. Invoke web browser with each of the IP addresses obtained in step 1 and
  3. Check and confirm which of those IP addresses result in the ‘successful reach to the IP address’

Few questions :

Q1. Steps 2 and 3 have to be automatically executed through the bash script, correct?

Q2. In which path are any of the web bowsers installed in the se2001.ds.study.iitm.ac.in? I checked /usr/bin/ but couldn’t find either ‘firefox’ or ‘chromium-browser’.

Q3. If I try executing ‘firefox’, I am being asked to install firefox, using the ‘apt install…’ command : Should I go ahead and install the browser?

Q4. Please give some clue or suggestion about which command to use to launch the web browser from within the bash script, such that, this command returns a value if it successfully reaches the site.

Q5. Any additional details on what exactly is being expected from the student, in the solution of this question, will be highly appreciated with thanks.

P.S : An unsolicited feedback : I am sure the wording of this question can be improved such that we as students, can learn something useful & relevant in say, the bash shell scripting & Linux, rather than sending us "on a wild-goose chase”. Humble request : Please review the effectiveness of this wording of the BPT1 question 4 w.r.t achieving the stated objectives of this course. Thanks!

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
24f1002419_IITM_MKS:

Q1. Steps 2 and 3 have to be automatically executed through the bash script, correct?

No, this is to be done from your local system, course VM does not have outbound network access.

24f1002419_IITM_MKS:

Q2. In which path are any of the web bowsers installed in the se2001.ds.study.iitm.ac.in? I checked /usr/bin/ but couldn’t find either ‘firefox’ or ‘chromium-browser’.

Q3. If I try executing ‘firefox’, I am being asked to install firefox, using the ‘apt install…’ command : Should I go ahead and install the browser?

Q4. Please give some clue or suggestion about which command to use to launch the web browser from within the bash script, such that, this command returns a value if it successfully reaches the site.

  • You don’t open browsers from inside the course VM, that of course is not possible over headless systems like a ssh connection, a browser window needs a display server like X or wayland server to be running.
  • There are no installed browsers because the VM is a headless VM.
  • You do not have superuser priviledges to install anything, neither are you expected to do so.

Perform nslookup on each domain from your system, get the IP, open them in browsers from your system and note if its same domain opening as the one we used with nslookup. Your script should simply print this answer as a series of Yes/No.

such as:

echo "www.google.com Yes"

posts.name: Subramanian M K (MKS)
posts.cooked:
First and foremost, heartfelt thanks for the prompt response. Your reply is helpful and clarified what is required.

Having said that, I have cut & pasted the contents of the README.md in /opt/se2001/BPT1_problem_4 below :

Please use the nslookup command (on powershell or linux on your local system) to identify the IP addresses associated with the following websites. ***After obtaining the IP addresses, enter each one into a browser to check if it directs you to the corresponding website. For each website, print the result using the echo command: if the website is successfully reached using the IP address, print “www.website.com Yes”, otherwise print “www.website.com No”. Perform these steps for each website sequentially:***

www.google.com



www.yahoo.com



www.duckduckgo.com



www.youtube.com



www.aws.amazon.com

Create a file with name `script.sh` which contains the `echo` commands sequentially.

Hint:

You can use the nslookup command for DNS lookup.

What is DNS and Why Perform a DNS Lookup?: The Domain Name System (DNS) translates human-readable domain names (like www.example.com) into IP addresses (like 93.184.216.34). DNS is crucial because it allows users to access websites using domain names instead of remembering complex IP addresses. A DNS lookup retrieves the IP address associated with a domain name, which is essential for network troubleshooting and ensuring that domain names are correctly mapped to their respective IP addresses.

Rather than pin pricking, I leave to the learned TAs and other course leaders to assess the above wording and conclude whether this could be improved.

Thanks again!
